overview: AntiCactus is a wire-silent geometry override: a single BlockBBEvent handler replaces every cactus's collision box with a full 1x1x1 block, so locally the cactus collides like any solid block and the player's bounding box never overlaps the cactus damage zone. The module sends no packets of its own; it shapes the movement the client reports, and the protection holds only while the reported C03 positions stay outside the server's thin cactus box. The hook is the fork's MixinBlock, which fires BlockBBEvent with the block's collision box and applies the event's mutated box.

sections.p: The handler matches event.block against BlockCactus and replaces event.boundingBox with a full cube from (x, y, z) to (x + 1, y + 1, z + 1). Vanilla cactus collision is a narrow central column, so normally a player walking into the cactus overlaps the damage box and BlockCactus.onEntityCollidedWithBlock applies damage. With the full cube in place the player collides with the phantom block face first, and local physics never push the bounding box into the damage zone.

The fork's MixinBlock overwrites addCollisionBoxesToList, firing BlockBBEvent with the block's collision box for every block whose box intersects the entity's AABB, then uses the event's mutated box for the actual collision test. That makes the event the single choke point for every block the player touches, which is why one small handler rewrites cactus behavior globally. LiquidSense Dev's snapshot has no net/minecraft tree, so the mixins directory is the mechanism home.

The module never calls sendPacket, so no anticheat sees the override directly; the effect is entirely local. Cactus damage is computed server-side from the server's own thin box against the server-side position, so the module only works while the client keeps its reported positions out of that box, which the full local box does by deflecting movement before the positions are sent. The C03 stream is the only thing the server sees, and it is shaped by the collision override.

files.label: AntiCactus.kt
files.explanation: The module is this 25-line Kotlin file: one @EventTarget handler on BlockBBEvent that replaces the bounding box with a full 1x1x1 cube whenever the block is a BlockCactus. It declares no settings, sends no packets, and holds no state; the entire mechanism is the box replacement on the event, which the fork's mixin applies to collision. The @ModuleInfo declaration registers it under the player category with the description 'Prevents cactuses from damaging you.'

files.label: MixinBlock.java (BlockBBEvent hook)
files.explanation: MixinBlock is the fork's overwrite of addCollisionBoxesToList: it fires BlockBBEvent with the block's collision box and then uses the event's mutated box for collision resolution against the entity. AntiCactus's full-cube replacement is applied through this mixin, so the file is the mechanism home for the module; LiquidSense Dev bundles no net/minecraft sources, and the mixins directory under net/ccbluex/liquidbounce/injection/forge is where the client's vanilla behavior modifications actually live.

countering.label: AntiCactusBerryCheck (proximity probe)
countering.explanation:
Jinky's AntiCactusBerryCheck is the only cactus-aware check in the entire corpus. On each PlayerMoveEvent it tests whether the player is within 0.31 blocks (x and z with offsets) of a cactus block and, when the player is not exempt with the 'damaged' reason, fails with 'cactus didn't hurt'. The check is a direct hit on the module's purpose: being next to a cactus without taking damage is exactly what AntiCactus produces, and no wire-silent geometry override can fake the damage event that the exemption requires.

The bypass surface is the geometric margin: the check fires at 0.31 blocks, so a player who keeps more distance or passes at speed may never sit inside the window long enough to accumulate a violation. The check also covers sweet berry bushes with age above zero, which is the same proximity-without-damage family.

countering.label: FabricatedMove (momentum disagreement)
countering.explanation:
FabricatedMove punishes position-bearing movement packets that report no delta while the server's velocity model says the player should still be moving, and separately flags more than 20 consecutive non-position updates. The knockback-into-cactus case is the module's tell: when the server pushes the player toward a cactus, the client-side phantom full box absorbs the collision, so the next position packet reports a zero delta while Hawk's velocity model still expects the knockback motion to resolve.

The check is a collateral channel rather than a cactus detector, which is the honest framing for a wire-silent module: it fires on the momentum disagreement the override creates, not on the cactus itself. A player who is never knocked back into a cactus never trips it.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (collision-model offsets)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed horizontal and vertical movement from the server's own collision model, and a client whose collision geometry disagrees with the server's produces offsets the envelope cannot explain. The client treats cactus as a full solid block while the server treats it as a thin column, so any knockback or piston push that the local collision redirects or absorbs lands as h and y deltas the server-side model never authorized, and the accumulated (max(hAbove, 0) + max(yAbove, 0)) * 100 violation returns a set-back.

State the boundary honestly: cactus damage itself is server-side (BlockCactus.onEntityCollidedWithBlock), so the envelope never sees the damage either. The check counters the movement side effects of the geometry disagreement, and the module only works at all while its reported positions stay out of the server's thin damage box.
